2334def flatten_curve(
2335    points: Sequence[PointType], n_points: int | None = None
2336) -> list[tuple[tuple[float, float], tuple[float, float]]]:
2337    """Sample a Bézier and join the samples with straight segments.
2338
2339    Samples are spaced evenly in ``t``. ``n_points`` is the number of
2340    samples, including both endpoints. The default is
2341    ``n_bezier_points``.
2342
2343    Examples:
2344        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2345        >>> lines = sg.flatten_curve([(0, 0), (40, 80), (80, 80), (60, 0)], n_points=5)
2346        >>> len(lines)
2347        4
2348        >>> [[round(c, 6) for c in lines[0][0]], [round(c, 6) for c in lines[0][1]]]
2349        [[0.0, 0.0], [29.0625, 45.0]]
2350        >>> [round(c, 6) for c in lines[-1][1]]
2351        [60.0, 0.0]
2352    """
2353    controls = _control_array(points)
2354    if n_points is None:
2355        n_points = runtime_defaults["n_bezier_points"]
2356    if len(controls) == 3:
2357        samples = q_bezier_points(controls[0], controls[1], controls[2], n_points)
2358    else:
2359        samples = bezier_points(
2360            controls[0], controls[1], controls[2], controls[3], n_points
2361        )
2362    vertices = [(float(sample[0]), float(sample[1])) for sample in samples]

2553def bezier_circle_intersections(
2554    points: Sequence[PointType],
2555    center: PointType,
2556    radius: float,
2557    tolerance: float = 0.01,
2558) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
2559    """Return intersections of a Bézier with a circle.
2560
2561    The curve is converted to arcs first. A curve that contains an arc of
2562    the circle raises ``ValueError``.
2563
2564    Examples:
2565        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2566        >>> hits = sg.bezier_circle_intersections(
2567        ...     [(0, 0), (10, 0), (20, 0), (30, 0)], (15, 0), 5
2568        ... )
2569        >>> [[round(c, 6) for c in hit] for hit in hits]
2570        [[10.0, 0.0], [20.0, 0.0]]
2571        >>> quarter = sg.circular_arc_beziers((0, 0), 10, 0, sg.pi / 2)[0]
2572        >>> sg.bezier_circle_intersections(quarter.control_points, (0, 0), 10)
2573        Traceback (most recent call last):
2574        ...
2575        ValueError: The curve lies on the circle.
2576        >>> cuts = sg.bezier_circle_intersections(quarter.control_points, (10, 10), 10)
2577        >>> [[round(c, 6) for c in hit] for hit in cuts]
2578        [[0.0, 10.0], [10.0, 0.0]]
2579    """
2580    if radius <= 0.0:
2581        raise ValueError("radius must be positive.")
2582    origin = _xy(center)
2583    query = BezierArc(
2584        (0.0, 0.0), (0.0, 0.0), origin, radius, 0.0, 2.0 * math.pi, False
2585    )
2586    hits: list[tuple[float, float]] = []
2587    for arc in bezier_to_arcs(points, tolerance):
2588        if arc.straight or arc.center is None:
2589            hits.extend(
2590                point
2591                for point in _segment_circle_hits(arc, query)
2592                if _point_on_arc(arc, point)
2593            )
2594            continue
2595        same = (
2596            _hypot(_sub(arc.center, origin)) <= 1.0e-5
2597            and abs(arc.radius - radius) <= 1.0e-5
2598        )
2599        if same:
2600            raise ValueError("The curve lies on the circle.")
2601        hits.extend(
2602            point
2603            for point in _circle_points(arc.center, arc.radius, origin, radius)
2604            if _point_on_arc(arc, point)
2605        )
2606    return _unique_points(hits)

2635def bezier_self_intersections(
2636    points: Sequence[PointType], tolerance: float = 0.01
2637) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
2638    """Return interior points where a Bézier crosses itself.
2639
2640    Adjacent fitted arcs share a joint, so those joints are not reported.
2641    A curve that starts and ends at the same point does not report that
2642    shared endpoint. Overlapping pieces raise ``ValueError``.
2643
2644    Examples:
2645        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2646        >>> sg.bezier_self_intersections([(0, 0), (40, 80), (40, -80), (0, 0)])
2647        []
2648        >>> sg.bezier_self_intersections([(0, 0), (30, 0), (30, 0), (0, 0)])
2649        Traceback (most recent call last):
2650        ...
2651        ValueError: The curve overlaps itself.
2652        >>> hits = sg.bezier_self_intersections([(0, 0), (80, 80), (-20, 80), (60, 0)])
2653        >>> [[round(c, 2) for c in hit] for hit in hits]
2654        [[30.0, 40.0]]
2655    """
2656    arcs = bezier_to_arcs(points, tolerance)
2657    hits: list[tuple[float, float]] = []
2658    try:
2659        for index, arc in enumerate(arcs):
2660            if index + 1 < len(arcs):
2661                hits.extend(
2662                    hit
2663                    for hit in _arc_hits(arc, arcs[index + 1])
2664                    if _hypot(_sub(hit, arc.end)) > 1.0e-4
2665                )
2666            for other in arcs[index + 2 :]:
2667                hits.extend(_arc_hits(arc, other))
2668    except ValueError:
2669        raise ValueError("The curve overlaps itself.") from None
2670    controls = _control_array(points)
2671    if _hypot(_sub(controls[0], controls[-1])) <= 1.0e-6:
2672        hits = [hit for hit in hits if _hypot(_sub(hit, controls[0])) > 1.0e-4]
2673    return _unique_points(hits)

def segmentize_catmull_rom(a: float, b: float, c: float, d: float, n: int = 100) -> Sequence[float]: 
2676def segmentize_catmull_rom(
2677    a: float, b: float, c: float, d: float, n: int = 100
2678) -> Sequence[float]:
2679    """a and b are the control points and c and d are
2680    start and end points respectively,
2681    n is the number of segments to generate.
2682
2683    Args:
2684        a (float): First control point.
2685        b (float): Second control point.
2686        c (float): Start point.
2687        d (float): End point.
2688        n (int, optional): Number of segments to generate. Defaults to 100.
2689
2690    Returns:
2691        Sequence[float]: List of points representing the segments.
2692
2693    Examples:
2694        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2695        >>> pts = sg.segmentize_catmull_rom((0, 0), (40, 0), (80, 40), (60, 0), n=2)
2696        >>> [[round(float(c), 6) for c in q[:2]] for q in pts]
2697        [[40.0, 0.0], [63.75, 22.5], [80.0, 40.0]]
2698    """
2699    a = array(a[:2], dtype=float)
2700    b = array(b[:2], dtype=float)
2701    c = array(c[:2], dtype=float)
2702    d = array(d[:2], dtype=float)
2703
2704    t = 0
2705    dt = 1.0 / n
2706    points = []
2707    term1 = 2 * b
2708    term2 = -a + c
2709    term3 = 2 * a - 5 * b + 4 * c - d
2710    term4 = -a + 3 * b - 3 * c + d
2711
2712    for _ in range(n + 1):
2713        q = 0.5 * (term1 + term2 * t + term3 * t**2 + term4 * t**3)
2714        points.append([q[0], q[1]])
2715        t += dt
2716    return points

a and b are the control points and c and d are start and end points respectively, n is the number of segments to generate.

Arguments:
  • a (float): First control point.
  • b (float): Second control point.
  • c (float): Start point.
  • d (float): End point.
  • n (int, optional): Number of segments to generate. Defaults to 100.
Returns:

Sequence[float]: List of points representing the segments.

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> pts = sg.segmentize_catmull_rom((0, 0), (40, 0), (80, 40), (60, 0), n=2)
>>> [[round(float(c), 6) for c in q[:2]] for q in pts]
[[40.0, 0.0], [63.75, 22.5], [80.0, 40.0]]

class SplineC(_BezierSpline): 
2898class SplineC(_BezierSpline):
2899    """A composite cubic Bezier curve.
2900
2901    The control points are given in walk order as
2902    ``[v0, c0, c1, v1, c2, c3, v2, ...]`` so each additional segment
2903    contributes two control points and an endpoint.
2904
2905    Examples:
2906        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
2907        >>> spline = sg.SplineC(
2908        ...     [(0, 0), (20, 40), (40, 40), (60, 0), (80, -40), (100, -40), (120, 0)],
2909        ...     n_points=9,
2910        ... )
2911        >>> len(spline.curves)
2912        2
2913        >>> [round(c, 6) for c in spline.point(0.0)]
2914        [0.0, 0.0]
2915        >>> [round(c, 6) for c in spline.point(1.0)]
2916        [120.0, 0.0]
2917    """
2918
2919    _stride = 3
2920    _segment_size = 4
2921    _subtype = Types.BEZIER
2922    _name = "SplineC"

A composite cubic Bezier curve.

The control points are given in walk order as [v0, c0, c1, v1, c2, c3, v2, ...] so each additional segment contributes two control points and an endpoint.

Examples:
>>> import simetri.graphics as sg
>>> spline = sg.SplineC(
...     [(0, 0), (20, 40), (40, 40), (60, 0), (80, -40), (100, -40), (120, 0)],
...     n_points=9,
... )
>>> len(spline.curves)
2
>>> [round(c, 6) for c in spline.point(0.0)]
[0.0, 0.0]
>>> [round(c, 6) for c in spline.point(1.0)]
[120.0, 0.0]
